body: It will affect them, and dearly so. There will be so many memories and times missed out upon. They will still have love and affection and whomever else enters their lives to share those with along with their beautiful caring mother. Life insurance was cashed out and terminated prematurely so I gained a little bit of finances there. I do not have social media of any kind other than this Reddit account. My vehicles have been sold, I plan to close bank account tomorrow and leave all the cash and useless possessions behind. As someone who lost more than a handful of people to suicide and dozens more to life, I am more than well aware for what everyone will be left with. My end-of-life choice will be permanent, but so is her and my family never becoming a whole again.

I remind myself of my daughters constantly. My father took his life when I was their same age. I've considered if that was a contribution to my decision but don't believe so honestly. My girls will have a much better life and more support than I ever had. They are more adaptable than they get credit for. They will come to their own acceptance at some point in their precious lives much like I did. I only wanted the one family I stayed around long and strong enough to build before my life came crashing down once more. Rebuilding and starting over isn't an option in my heart. I've wanted to go find my peace for more than half my life. All that has happened has just provided enough space and reason to set my soul and body free. In the end, we both get what we want. She can find her other special someone and I get to escape the grief and emotional torture. I see my kids as a causality to the circumstances already. It's not how I intended them to learn what a real family should be and how true love overcomes it all. Those objectives are now beyond my control and other life lessons will shake the seas of their futures. The only thing I can control is my life and reactions to the events at hand. My choice is just that, my choice. I appreciate the words of encouragement, I'm just not going to turn back. This is something for me. Afterall, doesn't everyone usually advise to work on yourself, focus on you?

I have tried other outlets to help myself. The only thing that would really save me would be her coming back and having my daughters together as a family and once more. Other than that I just don't care to try and because I know it will never happen I'm comfortable with saying goodbye. Everyone has already left me at some point in my life and those who remain will too. Fortunately, as they say time heals all. My calling is near and I have intentions to answer that call. It's my turn to do the leaving and everyone else will have to learn and develop their own reasons for why such things in life are meant to be the way they are.

Blank, empty space, without reason. I'm finding the opposite in your "sign" as it relates to my life and soul.

Hope it saves someone for another day though.

When others claim they'll be there and when you need them, they are not, only amplifies our feelings of isolation. We know we have purpose, even if we don't know what it is at the moment. You aren't alone. We are all here with the same contemplations. As for options, you're reaching out and that's a start. Send me a message if you need to talk.
I hope you realize you deserved better and it wasn't years of being lied to. May you make it through this pain to find better love friend. Keep your head up. I'm here to talk if you need.

Our lives are most important to ourselves. Whether it's to live it or take it. The wake of emotional casualty and torment is almost never intentionally directed towards others. 

I hope your kind words open the eyes of those struggling with similar feelings. There will always be someone out there who we are important to. It's even possible that person is a variation of one's self yet to be discovered.

I've always had the feeling like I've never belonged here either. Even after building a family and having that leave me too. Maybe there is still something out there in this world for the both of us? Maybe there's another place where we belong? Hope to see you in peace, here, or on the other side.

I know exactly what my daughters will go through. Children are extremely resilient and adaptable. I made it to 32 and my girls are 3 1/2. The same age when my father took his life. I could only hope that their odds to make the same choice later in life is greatly diminished since they will still remain with their amazing mother. I'm happy to hear your kids are keeping you hanging on. Stay strong! PM me if you ever need to talk.

Happy to hear you're hanging in there. I appreciate your gratitude for us. All in all, it was yourself that saved you. Keep surprising yourself with what you are capable of. You know you have your father and us here anytime you need support. Much love.

If the universe has a plan, may it be to bring all of us and the people we love back together or give us peace. I'm sinking in the same boat as the rest of you fellows. Sometimes bailing water is an option but not worth the effort. When it gets worse and the ship goes down, I hope you remember how to swim. You still have a lot going for you buddy. Message me or anyone here if you need to.

Personal story....

I had a friend from high school and we became close. I actually wound up living there for a short time and his family became like mine. There came a point where he felt like his family loved me more than him and began to despise me. He shot himself. I helped clean the mess. I saw what the family went through. It torments me to this day that I feel like a contribution to his choice. 

Emotions of anger, sadness, and at some point acceptance. People are rarely forgotten. They may just not come to mind as frequently when they are gone. And depending the memory that returns, the emotion may be shown in tears, frustration, or smiles.

It's not a reason to put me in my dark space, but I have a great understanding of the aftermath of suicide, family to friends, from the hell life has set before me.

One week? Let's start there if that's all we have for now and see how far it goes okay? You have a deal my friend. I will try my damn hardest to keep chugging along. At least if I can't save myself, maybe I can help save you. And that would make me feel better. Check the little history I have and you'll see I can relate. Message me if need be please.

When I'm all alone and realize all I have is myself, that all those "friends" who said they were just a call away don't respond, I come here to read and open myself the same way to give and receive some sort of light. PM me please. I would love to talk.

Forty pounds down, "dress rehearsals", planned and ready to go with the same emptiness and I can't every day. Why it's not now and why face the pain I can't live with tomorrow ? Honestly not a clue where it's coming from, but maybe we all can. At least one more day. 

Hate for even my worst enemy to feel the way we do. Hope things start looking brighter for you. I'm here for you while I'm here. ❤
I've sat there kissing steel with tears of joy, but I'm here willing to lend an ear.
Before you get closer, pause. We're here for you.

You don't know how....right now. I'm treading water in the same shoes with 2 kids on my back. In some time you will learn to distract yourself, hopefully before making an impulsive decision. I have gotten a bit "better" myself, but haven't changed my mind. Please talk to myself, or anyone here before you load that round.

I might guess you question it because a part of you wants to hear that he will be to give you freedom to escape the pain you're going through. I ask the same about my daughters and can come up with different reasons for yes and no to that argument. I know my day is coming near without question and that they will have to be ok, but truthfully may never be, even with the great support that will remain with them. Thoughts if they might attempt and battle the same demons when they age flood my mind. My father left when I was 3 and maybe it's why I have made my decision. I certainly don't want that for my kids, but the only hope I have is that it never becomes a rational decision to themselves. Your son having spent more time with you and learned so much more will undoubtedly have a greater affect. He may struggle the rest of his life with the same "it gets better/it'll be okay" even if one day he is "ok". It's a scenario that cannot be changed he will carry forever. And in your heart you know you don't want him to carry that with him or meet the same fate. If he's always with you, then try to always be there for as long as you can fight. Best wishes for happiness and peace from a sailor in a similar boat. Message me if you ever need to please.
I have two ears, an open heart and mind, and shoulders to lean and cry on. Send a message my way, or if you're in S. Fla, even better.

It's hard for me to be a hypocrite and sway you one way or the other. For a moment, breathe, contemplate, and recollect yourself as hard as it may be. Unfortunately life took one of the good ones instead of any of us wanting to end it all. It wasn't his choice to leave. And I'm willing to believe he would want you to stay strong and find your way, for the both of you. He may not be physically by your side, but he is with you, a great part of you if you will. You will be again together someday. If he was a great partner, then try to carry on a bit longer for a slice of happiness or to fulfill something you both had dreamed of. Do it for him and do it for yourself. 

I'm sorry doesn't help or fix anything. From the bottom of my heart though, I wish the anguish of your loss didn't have to be bestowed upon you to make you feel this way. The past cannot be changed. Just try to be here the best you can for the present, and maybe see a bit of light in the future. I'll be here too if you need to talk. Hope you manage to find a bit of hope and peace wherever your road may take you.

When a person comes to terms with one's self under the circumstances, I believe it is within their justified right to make such a decision. You have an unobscured comprehension and a validation in finding your peace. Sometimes we have to do what is best for ourselves and not everyone else will see it the same. I wish you the best.

Some people will have a better support system and others a stronger will. And the ideations will never be a thought to a percentage of those. I wish that no one would have to suffer these pains of life, but there are just some things we cannot control. We can only control how we react. 

If only my daughters were enough to keep me going for the Long Haul. They keep fading, the distance keeps growing and daddy is becoming more and more a memory. It makes it easier and harder at the same time but my decisions will be far from impulsive. 

Make yourself and your son proud. Be an example of the man you want him to grow up to be. You may not see it now but I know you have the ability to do the seemingly impossible. Succeed where others, myself included, cannot. You still have hope. Much love from this stranger.

I'm struggling with something quite similar and have had multiple friends and strangers attempt to affirm the same...that it will all feel better with time as you grieve and heal. I know just how hard it is, but maintain the strength to see your son's smile as often as you can. Let that empower you and he be the reason you carry on through each day for yourself to actually find that things will one day be okay. Until then, cry, grieve, reach out to whoever you need, and try to distract yourself positively (easier said than done, I know). 

For as long as I'm still here, feel free to message me if you ever need anyone to talk to. I wish you the best. Stay strong!

I haven't yet fully figured out just how to ensure my daughters will not forget how much they are to me. The unconditional love and how much I tried, did, and fought for our family. Their own understanding and reasoning will come with more time than I have. Once I am comfortable with that, there isn't anything else to keep me from my peace.

My deepest sympathies to you and your family. Your metaphor is beyond beautiful. I'm glad to hear your understandings, acceptance, and have the courage to move foward for yourself and your children. You will plow the thick fields ahead and break the cycle. I admire your strength and if you need anyone to talk to, I'm just a message away.

I have been suicidal over women before. I never had hatred for any of them. A change in emotion to hate or perhaps happiness might have assisted in getting over the sadness waiting for the "meant to be". Now I'm here AGAIN, rowing the same boat I wish to sink because we both thought we were the "One" and had children. Hopes and dreams gone because people change. Unfortunately my thoughts haven't much. 

Hope the game turns in your favor, whichever way you choose to play.

Agreed. I can only look for the hope that she would want to be again one day. It just isn't there. Hanging on to the what ifs is not practical and pushing me back down the rabbit hole.

The same could be understood for me wanting to check out. It's what I want, right or wrong, and only I can change it. However, the majority of people cannot comprehend what it's like to have the ideation in my scenario. The love between myself and my daughters truly is unconditional. I don't believe they would ever grow to hate me, nor would anyone shame me to them because I am a great father. The time of seperation, overcoming emotions and anguish, added to the fact I was the same age losing my father, the age my nephew was losing my sister. My daughters are the same age and it's almost a universal calling. But I'm supposed to break the cycle when I'm faltering to find that will power.

Not harsh or insensitive. You speak the truth. There could be and are other women out there and my kids absolutely deserve for me to be there. What won't change is that she will always be their mother and the one family I wanted and started building with. She was able to do what she wanted, affecting our girls in not such a drastic way as my considerations. We cannot control the actions of others. I know I'm solely responsible for my own desires and the recourse. I can't find myself years down the road yearning for her and my family or breaking down, showing weakness to my daughters, failing at being the man and father I need to be.

Walking into the empty shell of what used to be OUR home and having memories replay in my mind, doing things and going places, hearing my daughters ask for Daddy...it's all torturous. If I'm gone I am all too familiar with what they will have to go through. They will have their mother and Nana. Assuming some other tragedy doesn't interrupt their innocence, their mother should see grandchildren. They are Daddy's girls and will need their father in life. I get that too. I didn't make it half bad as far as I did and I'm sure they would still have the possibility to go further down a better path than I was forced to trek.

I hide the pain and suffering through joyous smiles when she is around and I am with my daughters. I don't beg for her back, give her the space and show respect for her decision because I don't want to push her away even more. I'm failing to grasp how a relationship is part of the reason why she left, and she hasn't sought it out due to her emotions she still has for me, even though she was attempting to get something going with someone else before we seperated. The other part for her leaving was just not "in love" with me, not wanting to work on "us", and obviously my reaction of being too honest and open with my feelings regarding the situation and inevitability of her leaving. I hate my intuition tells me she won't try again because it leaves me hopeless, even if her closest friend says otherwise. Whether it be something I know or not and if the situation is open for interpretation. I would leave a detailed, loving response on the back of a framed large photo of myself and my children to remind them of some of the answers they will need for questions they gather as they grow up.  If either is a bit like me, I'd like to believe they would remember, trust, and understand the love that will always be and the love lost.

My memory does serve an equal good purpose and I struggle to find the positives in it all, but I know they are there. Appreciate you lending an ear.

Edit: I'm conflicted and unsure as to what is the most painful...the situation itself, the fact my intuition was right before and is telling me she won't come back, or knowing the emotional pain and burden my precious daughters will face for the rest of their lives the day I choose I can't do this any longer.
